domain_restrictions: n is an integer and satisfies n > 1
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n - 1
x and y are real numbers satisfying m/n <= x <= y and y < (m+1)/n
the upper endpoint (m+1)/n is excluded for y, and therefore also excluded for x because x <= y
k in the sum is an integer with 1 <= k <= n (so division by k is by a nonzero integer)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1, the function Fn defined by Fn(t) = floor(n t) minus sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k t) divided by k is nonincreasing on each interval [m/n, (m+1)/n) in the sense that for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1 and for all real x and y with m/n <= x <= y < (m+1)/n, one has Fn(x) >= Fn(y).
quantifier_order: for all integers n greater than 1
for all integers m with 0 <= m <= n-1
for all real numbers x and y with m/n <= x <= y and y < (m+1)/n

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter defining the function Fn

variables.name: m
variables.role: chooses one subinterval of the real line

variables.domain: real numbers with m/n <= x <= y and x < (m+1)/n
variables.name: x
Fn
variables.role: maps a real t to floor(n t) minus sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k t) divided by k

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index inside the definition of Fn

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; all quantified variables (n, m, x, y) are universal.
Fn depends on n, and the sum in Fn depends on n through its upper limit n.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For any integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1 and any real numbers x,y satisfying m/n <= x <= y < (m+1)/n, one has F_n(x) >= F_n(y).
